signals.title: NZD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + ESI Divergence
signals.text: NZD/JPY remains the focal point of a massive G10 performance gap as the JPY 1W average hits +1.955% against a sagging NZD at -1.669%. The 3.624% spread is driven by the BoJ chief's signal that rate hikes remain on the table for this month's meeting, directly supporting the JPY 1.0% vs RBNZ 2.75% narrowing yield narrative. While NZD positioning is at a 52-week low (pctl 0, z -2.60), JPY data is outperforming with an ESI of +27.9 compared to NZD's neutral -3.1. The bilateral theme is reinforced by the JPY safe-haven bid returning as Asian markets trade mixed ahead of US NFP. Technical resistance for JPY strength (downside for NZD/JPY) is anchored by the USD/JPY SMA200 at 158.45. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/JPY; JPY outperformance theme dominates G10 flows. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — hike bias building. Risk: NZD short-squeeze on an unexpected hawkish RBNZ shift before October.

signals.title: USD/JPY — BoJ Hawkish Shift + Vol Complacency
signals.text: USD/JPY is testing 157.01, trading below its SMA20 at 159.17 and SMA50 at 160.71 following BoJ chief Ueda's comments that rate hikes are possible at every meeting. Despite the 275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage supporting the pair at a policy level, the options market exhibits unusual complacency with USD/JPY IV at 7.2% vs HV30 of 10.4%, creating a -3.2% VRP. This negative volatility risk premium suggests the market is underpricing downside risk, even as 25d risk reversals show a strong -1.82 put skew for downside protection. A correlation break (z=+1.91σ) vs VIX indicates JPY is no longer purely tracking equities, instead reacting to domestic policy repricing. SMA200 at 158.45 now acts as immediate resistance on any recovery attempt. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; policy convergence outweighs carry while VRP remains negative. Catalyst: US NFP report tomorrow. Risk: Strong US jobs data re-widens yield spreads, overriding BoJ verbal signals.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD is holding at 0.7170, positioned above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.6981–0.7120), yet faces significant positioning headwinds. COT Leveraged Fund net long is at +53,578, which sits in the 95th percentile (z +1.92) of its 52-week range, signaling a crowded institutional long. This is contrasted by extreme retail sentiment, where 86% of retail traders are short, creating a massive institutional vs retail divergence. While the 60bp AUD carry premium vs USD (RBA 4.35% vs Fed 3.75%) remains a structural support, the combination of a crowded COT long and moderate IV premium (VRP +1.1%) suggests limited upside room for a further chase. A failure to hold the SMA20 at 0.7120 would confirm a positioning-led pullback. Trade bias: Neutral/Caution AUD/USD; institutional crowding caps further upside. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep — 100% hold priced. Risk: Broad US Dollar weakness persists, forcing retail capitulation and an institutional extension higher.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Hedging Demand + ESI Misses
signals.text: GBP/USD is trading at 1.3497, sandwiched between its SMA20 resistance (1.3550) and SMA50 support (1.3442). While the Fed 3.75% vs BoE 3.75% spread is carry-neutral, the GBP Economic Surprise Index (ESI) has drifted to -8.7, indicating consistent data misses relative to USD's -12.8. Options markets are pricing in a significant 6.2-point Vol Risk Premium (IV 11.0% vs HV30 4.8%), the highest in the G10 space, signaling intense demand for protection despite the pair holding a mildly bullish bias near 1.3500. COT positioning remains historically high (pctl 96, z +1.58), but the lack of carry premium makes this long position vulnerable to any further domestic data deterioration. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD; high vol premium reflects uncertainty despite positive price action. Catalyst: BoE meeting 17 Sep — 100% hold priced. Risk: A clean break below the SMA50/200 cluster at 1.3442 triggers a liquidation of crowded speculative longs.
